card.name: Kartuli
card.tagline: Georgia's lyrical, untouching wedding couple dance
card.profile: Kartuli is the romantic couple or wedding dance considered the crown jewel of Georgian choreography, without strong regional markers (Wikipedia; georgia.travel). During the dance the man may not touch the woman or even her clothing and must keep a precise distance, his upper body motionless, his gaze fixed on her - expressing controlled feeling and respect; the woman keeps her eyes downcast and glides 'as a swan on the smooth surface of a lake.' Conceived as a theatrical synthesis in the 11th-12th centuries, it follows a 6/8 rhythm and unfolds in parts (invitation, duet, the woman's solo, finale) (hobbyblendfun).
card.insight: Kartuli encodes the social code of the Georgian gender ideal - restraint, dignity and reverence for women - and in 2020 was designated a Monument of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Georgia (tbilisitrips).
card.image_significance: Couple wedding dance; he never touches her. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — national, Georgia.
